title: 1994 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Points \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C\) on a circle of radius \(r\) are situated so that \(AB=AC,\) \(AB\gt r,\) and the length of minor arc \(\widehat{BC}\) is \(r.\) If angles are measured in radians, then \(\frac{AB}{BC}=\)

solutions.text: The central angle subtending minor arc \(\widehat{BC}\) is \(\frac{r}{r}=1,\) so \(BC=2r\sin\frac12.\) Since \(AB=AC\) and \(AB\gt r,\) point \(A\) is the midpoint of the major arc \(BC.\) The minor central angle from \(A\) to \(B\) is \(\pi-\frac12,\) so \(AB=2r\)\(\sin\left(\frac{\pi-\frac{1}{2}}{2}\right)=2r\cos\frac14.\) Therefore \(\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{\cos(\frac{1}{4})}{\sin(\frac{1}{2})}\)\(=\frac1{2\sin(\frac{1}{4})}=\frac12\csc\frac14.\) Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: The minor arc \(\widehat{BC}\) subtends a central angle of \(1\) radian
Use the chord formula \(2r\sin(\frac{\theta}{2})\) for both \(BC\) and \(AB\)
